evals.prompt: I'm starting work on a new feature. Run pulse:preflight to check whether my environment is ready for the Pulse workflow.
evals.expected_output: Agent checks git, br, bv, and coordination runtime availability; writes .pulse/tooling-status.json with PASS/DEGRADED/FAIL and a recommended_mode; presents a clear status summary; and reports onboarding blockers honestly instead of claiming readiness when onboarding cannot be verified.
expectations: Agent attempts to check for git, br, and bv tool availability
Agent writes or describes writing .pulse/tooling-status.json
Agent reports both an overall PASS/DEGRADED/FAIL outcome and a recommended_mode
Agent reports onboarding blockers honestly and does NOT claim the environment is ready when onboarding cannot be verified or applied
Agent does NOT immediately start implementing features or creating beads

evals.prompt: I just ran preflight and it passed. I want to add a dark mode toggle to our React app. What Pulse skill should I use next and why?
evals.expected_output: Agent consults the skill catalog, identifies the request as a new feature with fuzzy decisions, routes to pulse:brainstorming or pulse:exploring, and explains the routing decision with the go-mode pipeline context.
expectations: Agent routes the user to pulse:brainstorming or pulse:exploring as the next step
Agent references the Pulse skill catalog or routing table
Agent does NOT jump directly to planning or executing
Agent explains why the chosen skill is appropriate for a new feature request

evals.prompt: I want to add a notification system to my app. Help me brainstorm how to approach this.
evals.expected_output: Agent asks ONE clarifying question at a time (not a batch), eventually proposes 2-3 approaches with trade-offs, presents a design for approval, writes a spec doc, runs self-review, and hands off to pulse:exploring. Does NOT write code.
expectations: Agent asks clarifying questions one at a time, not in a batch
Agent proposes 2-3 distinct approaches with trade-offs
Agent does NOT write any code or create beads during brainstorming
Agent identifies the terminal state as handing off to pulse:exploring

evals.prompt: I want to add user authentication with OAuth to our Node.js API. Let's explore what decisions we need to lock before planning.
evals.expected_output: Agent classifies scope, asks sequential Socratic questions (one at a time), assigns decision IDs (D1, D2...), and writes history/<feature>/CONTEXT.md. Does NOT start planning or create beads.
expectations: Agent asks questions one at a time with a HARD-GATE between each
Agent assigns stable decision IDs (D1, D2, etc.) as decisions are locked
Agent outputs or describes writing history/<feature>/CONTEXT.md
Agent does NOT create beads, write code, or invoke pulse:planning prematurely

evals.prompt: Make this prompt better: 'fix the login bug'
evals.expected_output: Agent transforms the vague prompt into a structured, execution-ready version with Objective, Context, Tool Rules, Output Contract, and Done Criteria blocks. Explains what changed.
expectations: Agent produces a significantly more structured and detailed version of the input prompt
Agent includes at least 3 of the framework blocks (Objective, Context, Tool Rules, Output Contract, Verification, Done Criteria)
Agent explains what was changed and why
Output is clearly more actionable than the original 'fix the login bug'

evals.prompt: Use pulse:gitnexus to find all files related to authentication in the current codebase and give me an architecture snapshot.
evals.expected_output: Agent checks the scout or dependency report for GitNexus readiness, uses GitNexus tools when configured (or rg fallback otherwise), summarizes architecture findings, and notes where results are saved (discovery.md).
expectations: Agent checks for GitNexus availability before running discovery commands
Agent uses GitNexus tools (query, context, impact, route analysis) or falls back to rg if unavailable
Agent produces an architecture summary or discovery notes
Agent saves or describes saving findings to history/<feature>/discovery.md

evals.prompt: Exploring is complete, `history/auth-oauth/CONTEXT.md` exists, and the scout says GitNexus is not configured for this repo/session. Run pulse:planning and determine whether planning can proceed.
evals.expected_output: Agent reads CONTEXT.md and critical-patterns.md, checks the scout or dependency report, continues Phase 1 discovery with explicit rg/file-inspection fallback when GitNexus is unavailable, and preserves the later approval-before-bead-creation gate.
expectations: Agent checks the scout or dependency report for GitNexus readiness before discovery
Agent does not stop planning solely because GitNexus is unavailable; it documents the fallback and continues with local inspection
Agent checks .pulse/memory/critical-patterns.md for institutional learnings
Agent preserves the approval gate before any bead creation if planning later proceeds

evals.prompt: Planning is done, the selected shape artifact is APPROVED, the current-work artifact exists, and the bead set contains a mix of valid and malformed behavior contracts. Run pulse:validating to determine whether the current work is execution-ready.
evals.expected_output: Agent orients from the selected shape, current-work artifact, and `.pulse/STATE.md`; scans beads for the canonical schema and mode-specific behavior evidence; identifies malformed beads; fails fast before any execution-ready verdict; and does not start implementation.
expectations: Agent performs an actual bead schema scan and identifies missing required fields in malformed beads
Agent fails fast on schema violations instead of proceeding to execution-ready
Agent reads approval status from the selected work-shape, phase-plan, or epic-map artifact and verifies the current-work slice
Agent validates behavior_mode and its behavior_steps or investigation_steps evidence
Agent does NOT start implementing beads itself

evals.prompt: Validating passed and execution is approved. Run pulse:swarming to coordinate the worker agents for this phase.
evals.expected_output: Agent confirms swarm readiness, uses the active runtime's native subagent primitives, spawns bounded workers running pulse:executing, monitors the bead graph and active coordination surface, enforces shared file reservations, and never directly implements beads itself.
expectations: Agent uses the active runtime's native subagent primitives without inventing a second coordination runtime
Agent spawns worker subagents running pulse:executing (not implementing beads directly)
Agent monitors worker state, the bead graph, and the active coordination surface
Agent checks or enforces shared file reservations before overlapping edits
Agent updates or describes updating .pulse/STATE.md with worker tracking

evals.prompt: I'm a worker agent. Run pulse:executing in single-worker mode to implement the next available bead.
evals.expected_output: Agent determines it is in single-worker mode, reads the bead graph via `bv --robot-priority`, claims the top bead, reads the full behavior contract and locked decisions, checks reservations, captures the declared baseline, implements the smallest credible intervention, runs retest/regression verification, records evidence, commits per bead, and loops.
expectations: Agent determines execution mode (single-worker vs swarm worker)
Agent uses bv --robot-priority (or describes using it) to claim the next bead
Agent reads the full bead including learning_refs before implementing
Agent follows behavior_mode with baseline, retest, and regression evidence without requiring a specific development ceremony
Agent checks file reservations before editing
Agent commits after each bead and writes verification evidence

evals.prompt: Execution is complete for the OAuth feature. Run pulse:reviewing to verify quality before merge.
evals.expected_output: Agent runs 4-5 specialist review agents (code quality, architecture, security, tests, synthesis), converts findings to P1/P2/P3 review beads, performs artifact verification, runs UAT against CONTEXT.md decisions, and blocks merge on P1s.
expectations: Agent spawns or describes spawning multiple specialist review agents (at least code quality, security, tests)
Agent creates review beads for findings with P1/P2/P3 severity
Agent performs artifact verification (checking verification files exist and are substantive)
Agent blocks merge if P1 beads exist and requires them to be resolved first

evals.prompt: The OAuth feature is merged. Run pulse:compounding to capture what we learned.
evals.expected_output: Agent gathers context from feature history/beads/reviews, runs pattern/decision/failure analysis, writes learning files under .pulse/memory/learnings/, promotes only global rules to .pulse/memory/critical-patterns.md, and updates STATE.md.
expectations: Agent gathers context from feature history, review findings, and debug notes
Agent analyzes through pattern, decision, and failure lenses
Agent writes learning files to .pulse/memory/learnings/ with domain/severity/propagation metadata
Agent only promotes genuinely global patterns to critical-patterns.md, not everything

evals.prompt: A worker is stuck: the OAuth callback test is failing with 'Cannot read property token of undefined'. Investigate it with pulse:systematic-debug-fix.
evals.expected_output: Agent frames the work as a single-issue investigation, reproduces the failure with the exact command, states an explicit root-cause hypothesis, traces the failure back to the original trigger, and defines the regression coverage needed so the bug does not return.
expectations: Agent frames the work as a single issue before editing code
Agent reproduces the failure before proposing a fix
Agent identifies and states a clear root-cause hypothesis
Agent calls for regression coverage that would fail without the fix

evals.prompt: There are 3 known bugs in the payment module: (1) double-charge on retry, (2) webhook signature validation failing on some providers, (3) refund amount rounding error. Fix them systematically.
evals.expected_output: Agent creates a tracker with all 3 issues, sequences them by dependency, investigates each before fixing, verifies each fix with a narrow test, adds regression coverage, and reports status for all items.
expectations: Agent creates an issue tracker listing all 3 bugs with IDs and status
Agent investigates (reproduces + traces root cause) before applying any fix
Agent applies fixes one at a time and verifies each individually
Agent adds regression tests or coverage for each fixed bug

evals.prompt: I want to create a new Pulse skill called 'pulse:dependency-audit' that automatically audits npm dependencies for security issues. Use pulse:writing-pulse-skills and evaluate whether local skill guidance improves behavior.
evals.expected_output: Agent freezes pressure scenarios and scoring, records the exact model/profile, runs BASELINE without the candidate skill, applies an INTERVENTION only for guidance-attributable gaps, then runs RETEST on the same cases and records results. A passing baseline causes no intervention. The process is documented in CREATION-LOG.md.
expectations: Agent freezes pressure scenarios and scoring before observing outcomes
Agent records the exact model and reasoning profile for BASELINE and RETEST
Agent applies an INTERVENTION only when BASELINE exposes a guidance-attributable gap
Agent reruns the same cases in RETEST and records improvements and regressions
Agent makes no intervention when BASELINE already passes and documents the evaluation in CREATION-LOG.md

evals.prompt: Run pulse:dream to consolidate learnings from recent Pulse work into the knowledge base.
evals.expected_output: Agent detects bootstrap vs recurring mode, selects runtime-aware sources for Claude, Codex, or mixed runs, extracts durable candidates, routes each into learning/correction/ratchet/pending/skip outcomes, updates memory files with provenance, queues ambiguous items only in explicitly non-blocking mode under .pulse/memory/dream-pending/, and never auto-edits critical-patterns.md without approval.
expectations: Agent detects whether this is a bootstrap-first or recurring consolidation run
Agent selects runtime-aware evidence sources for Claude, Codex, or mixed runs
Agent extracts durable candidates and routes them into learning, correction, ratchet, pending, or skip outcomes
Agent writes provenance markers when updating memory files
Agent does NOT auto-edit critical-patterns.md — requires explicit approval for promotions

evals.prompt: We just figured out that the checkout bug was really a stale-closure issue, not a bad API response. Use pulse:dev-note to save that learning into our dev notes.
evals.expected_output: Agent loads the raw note templates, captures one concrete reusable learning into the daily raw note file, avoids transcript dumping, and asks a short clarification question only if the intended learning is ambiguous.
expectations: Agent reads or references the hard raw-note templates before writing markdown
Agent captures a reusable learning rather than a broad transcript or task log
Agent writes or describes writing to dev-notes/raws/YYYYMMDD.md only
Agent asks a short clarification question if the desired learning is ambiguous instead of guessing

evals.prompt: We have a pile of pending raw dev notes now. Use pulse:dev-note-distil to turn them into stable topic knowledge and refresh the topic index.
evals.expected_output: Agent loads the topic and TOC templates, distills pending raw notes into stable topic files, merges into existing topics when the core idea overlaps, rebuilds TOPICS.md, and avoids inventing conclusions beyond the raw-note evidence.
expectations: Agent reads or references the hard topic and topics-index templates before writing markdown
Agent merges into existing topics when the core lesson overlaps instead of fragmenting the taxonomy
Agent rebuilds or describes rebuilding dev-notes/distil/TOPICS.md after topic updates
Agent keeps the distilled conclusions grounded in the underlying raw notes

evals.prompt: I'm starting Pulse in a repo with stale onboarding. The onboarding check reports changes to AGENTS.md and .codex hooks, but the user is offline. Run pulse:preflight to assess what needs to change and tell me exactly what you would say back to the user right now.
evals.expected_output: Agent runs the onboarding check command, reports status/actions, keeps the wrapper read-only by default, explicitly refuses apply without approval, explains preservation guarantees, and says planning/execution must not continue while onboarding is still unresolved unless the user declines.
expectations: Agent runs or describes running the onboarding check command against the repo root
Agent summarizes the onboarding status using actions and/or relevant details
Agent explicitly says the onboarding wrapper is read-only by default and refuses apply without approval
Agent explains at least two preservation guarantees, including the compact_prompt replacement boundary when confirmation is required
Agent says planning or execution must not continue while status is needs_onboarding unless the user declines or approves the remediation path
Agent does NOT apply repo changes without explicit user approval

evals.prompt: Exploring is complete for a durable regulated payments API and `history/payments-api/CONTEXT.md` is approved. No governance classification or governance.md exists because I invoked pulse:planning directly. Continue planning through Gate 2 setup.
evals.expected_output: Before creating a shape or requesting Gate 2, the agent invokes pulse:governed-feature, records an explicit strong|light|none Governance Fitness decision and rationale in approach.md, and for this strong-fit API/compliance change creates and structurally validates the single governance.md overlay.
expectations: Agent does not treat a missing governance overlay as an implicit light or none classification
Agent invokes pulse:governed-feature and records Governance Fitness: strong with a rationale in approach.md
Agent requires history/payments-api/governance.md and the passing bundled validator result before shape creation
Agent does not request or approve Gate 2 until the strong governance route is complete
